title: Notification is still delivered live when BullMQ/Redis is unavailable (direct-emit fallback)
description: Regression guard for NOTIF-002: before this fix, a Redis outage meant queue.add() threw and no delivery path existed, so notifications were silently DB-only until the next manual poll. dispatch() must keep calling getIo() directly when job is null.
preconditions: Target user has an active Socket.IO connection
steps: Dispatch a notification to the connected user
expectedResult: The connected client still receives the 'notification' socket event in real time via the fallback direct-emit path — this must not regress to DB-only silent delivery.

title: Socket reconnects automatically after NextAuth rotates the access token
description: Regression guard for NOTIF-004: a prior version left the socket authenticated with a stale token forever once NextAuth issued a new one, and connect_error handling used to forcibly disconnect on any JWT error, defeating the recovery path. The fix pushes the fresh token into socketRef.current.auth and calls .connect() if disconnected, and connect_error no longer force-disconnects.
preconditions: A session long-lived enough for NextAuth to rotate session.accessToken (or simulate by forcing a token refresh)
steps: Stay logged in until (or force) the NextAuth session token rotates
Observe the existing socket connection's auth token and connection state before/after rotation
expectedResult: The socket's auth.token is updated to the new value; if it had disconnected, it reconnects automatically without requiring the user to reload the page.

title: Notifications and scan-relevant emits target the org-scoped room, not just the bare user room
description: Regression guard for NOTIF-005: prior to this fix, delivery only used room user:{userId}, which meant a user who belongs to multiple organizations could receive notifications intended for a different org context than the one they're currently viewing. Both the worker and the direct-emit fallback must emit to org:{organizationId}:user:{targetUserId}.
preconditions: A user belongs to two organizations, Org A and Org B, and is connected with an Org A session
steps: Dispatch a notification targeting this user under organizationId = Org B (simulating a stale/multi-org membership)
Observe whether the Org-A-connected socket receives it
expectedResult: The socket, joined only to org:{OrgA}:user:{userId} (plus the bare user:{userId} room), does not receive the Org-B-scoped emit intended for a different org room — confirming org-room isolation holds for both the async worker path and the direct-emit fallback.

title: markAllRead exists and correctly normalizes isRead to read for the local unread filter
description: Regression guard for NOTIF-006: markAllRead was previously missing entirely from NotificationContext, and separately the local unreadCount filter (!n.read) silently stayed wrong for API-fetched notifications because only `isRead` was ever set, never `read`. Both markAsRead and markAllRead must set { isRead: true, read: true } locally.
preconditions: User has several unread notifications loaded in NotificationContext
steps: Inspect the notifications array in React state (e.g. via devtools) immediately after
expectedResult: Every notification object has both isRead:true and read:true, and unreadCount (computed as notifications.filter(n => !n.read).length) drops to 0 without requiring a re-fetch.

title: Cancelling scan SCAN-12 never incorrectly matches/cancels the progress entry for SCAN-1
description: Regression guard for NOTIF-008: the scan-cancelled handler's key-matching logic must only accept a stored progress key that STARTS WITH the incoming baseScanId (prefix match in one direction). A naive substring/reverse-prefix check previously risked SCAN-1 matching SCAN-12's cancellation.
preconditions: activeScanProgress state contains both SCAN-1 and SCAN-12 as running scans
steps: Emit a scan-cancelled event with { scanId: 'SCAN-12' }
Inspect activeScanProgress for both SCAN-1 and SCAN-12 afterward
expectedResult: Only the SCAN-12 entry (or its provider-suffixed variant, e.g. SCAN-12-aws) transitions to status='cancelled'; SCAN-1 remains in its prior running state, untouched.

title: The 60-second cross-tab read-state poll interval remains active in NotificationContext
description: Regression guard for NOTIF-010: NotificationContext registers setInterval(fetchNotifications, 60_000) specifically to catch read-state changes made in other browser tabs, given there is no push-based cross-tab sync. Removing or breaking this interval (e.g. during a refactor to React Query) would leave stale unread counts indefinitely in background tabs.
preconditions: Two tabs open with the same user session
steps: Mark a notification read in Tab 1
Wait at least 60-65 seconds without interacting with Tab 2
Check Tab 2's bell badge / NotificationMenu state
expectedResult: Tab 2 reflects the read state (bell badge decremented) after the poll interval elapses, confirming the interval is still wired up and firing on schedule.

title: NotificationMenu click-through uses notification.navigateTo, not a nonexistent 'link' field
description: Regression guard for NOTIF-011: an earlier version of NotificationMenu.js referenced notification.link, which the backend never populates (the field is navigateTo), silently making click-to-navigate a no-op for every notification.
preconditions: A notification with a populated navigateTo value, e.g. '/audit-assurance/123/configured'
expectedResult: The browser navigates to the navigateTo URL — this must not regress to reading a 'link' field that is always undefined.

title: NotificationMenu's getNotificationColor switch cases do not match any value in the real NOTIFICATION_TYPES enum
description: OPEN GAP (not yet fixed): NotificationMenu.js's getNotificationColor() switches on 'evidence_rejected', 'deadline_approaching', 'review_reminder', and 'evidence_approved' to pick red/orange/green — but notification.model.js's actual NOTIFICATION_TYPES enum is task_assigned, task_reassigned, task_due_soon, task_overdue, review_requested, review_approved, review_rejected, audit_invitation, scan_completed, escalation_required, general, sync_failed. None of the switch cases can ever match a real notificationType, so every notification renders with the default blue.500 regardless of urgency (e.g. an 'escalation_required' or 'task_overdue' item looks identical to a routine 'general' one). This case documents the current defect so a future refactor of either the enum or the color map doesn't silently 'fix' one side while leaving the mismatch on the other.
preconditions: Notifications exist with notificationType values 'task_overdue' and 'escalation_required'
steps: Open NotificationMenu and inspect the rendered title color for each
expectedResult: Current (defective) behavior: both render in the default blue.500 color, not visually distinguished from a routine 'general' notification, despite being high-urgency types. Flagged for remediation — the switch statement's case values should be reconciled with NOTIFICATION_TYPES.
